# Sentinel getting started

Sentinel passively audits your public estate every morning, watches for threats that touch your stack, and stays silent when nothing changed.

## Intake (one short question at a time, about 15 minutes)
Ask, adapting to answers; skip anything already known:
1. Company name.
2. Primary domain.
3. Known subdomains (app, api, admin, staging, dev, docs, status). Completeness not required; certificate logs fill gaps.
4. Key public endpoints: API base, login page, MCP server, webhook receivers, public API.
5. Public code: GitHub/GitLab org, public repos, npm/PyPI packages.
6. Data services: storage buckets, CDN, Supabase/Firebase project URLs.
7. Stack: languages, frameworks, cloud/hosting, database, auth, payments, email, protocols (MCP, OAuth, WebRTC).
8. Extended stack: tech customers or supply chain run that you host, connect to, or support (optional).
9. Where alerts go: this chat by default; any outside channel only with the owner's explicit yes per post.

## After intake
1. Save each answer as a private memory. Remind the owner the filled worksheet is confidential.
2. Run one full passive pass of the audit checklist and draft the BASELINE: open findings (with severity and fix path), verified-good tripwires, and what is explicitly untested (row-level security, login/OTP abuse, authenticated authorization, anything needing an account).
3. Have the owner review the baseline line by line; save it to memory once approved.
4. Create routines: daily estate audit 07:00 local, threat digests 08:00 and 18:00 local, and a frequent P1 check that stays silent unless P1.
5. Never start daily diffs before the baseline is reviewed.

Rules of engagement always apply: passive only, no fuzzing, no logins, no exploits, verify by content not status codes.
